chosen.premise: Bird Pokémon eggs are Ekans's favorite food, but swallowing one whole can leave it stuck and make it faint.
chosen.hook: Ekans loves eggs so much they can knock it out.
chosen.visualIdea: An egg slides down Ekans's throat, gets visibly wedged, and Ekans topples over with cartoon stars.
chosen.note: A favorite food becoming a literal knockout hazard is a sharp, memorable contradiction. The Ultra Moon entry directly supports the egg getting stuck and Ekans fainting.

candidates.premise: A newborn Ekans has no poison: its bite hurts, but it is harmless until it grows older.
candidates.hook: Baby Ekans is Poison-type—but its bite starts out harmless.
candidates.visualIdea: A hatchling Ekans bites a target with a pain icon but no poison effect, contrasted with an older-looking silhouette.
candidates.note: A Poison-type whose newborn bite is harmless is an excellent contradiction and clearly supported, though the exact transition into having poison is not described beyond the newborn stage.

candidates.premise: Ekans can dislocate its jaw to swallow prey larger than itself—then become too heavy to move.
candidates.hook: Ekans can win dinner… and immediately lose the ability to move.
candidates.visualIdea: Ekans unhinges its jaw around an oversized silhouette; a full belly drops it motionless onto the ground.
candidates.note: The immobility consequence gives the familiar snake-swallowing mechanic a concrete payoff, but jaw dislocation and oversized meals are not especially Ekans-exclusive.

candidates.premise: Ekans sleeps curled into a spiral so it can raise its head and respond to threats from any direction.
candidates.hook: Ekans sleeps in a shape designed to defend every side.
candidates.visualIdea: Top-down spiral Ekans as threat arrows arrive from all sides; its head pops up and glares toward each one.
candidates.note: The defensive resting shape is concrete and animates well, but coiling up to react defensively is fairly intuitive for a snake Pokémon.

candidates.premise: Ekans is 2 meters long but weighs only 6.9 kilograms—and it grows longer as it gets older.
candidates.visualIdea: A 2-meter measuring tape stretches beside Ekans, then a scale lands at 6.9 kg as its body extends with age.
candidates.note: The measurements are concrete and potentially striking in comparison, but size-and-weight trivia is not a character-specific premise and needs a stronger real-world visual benchmark.

candidates.premise: Ekans flicks its tongue to find prey by scent—and can also sense danger around it.
candidates.hook: Ekans's tongue is basically its danger radar.
candidates.visualIdea: Invisible scent trails and danger waves become visible only when Ekans flicks its tongue through tall grass.
candidates.note: The evidence is solid and scent trails are visual, but tongue-based environmental sensing is a broad snake trait rather than a distinctly Ekans story.

rounds.request: None needed; egg-stuck-faint is strong enough. A still stronger version would add a clear scale comparison for the egg versus Ekans's throat while keeping the official fainting consequence as the punchline.
